correctness.rationale: For connected diameter-at-most-two graphs, high colors cannot repeat and each broadcasts universally. A witnessing partition with fewer high-color roots than blocks forces exactly one rootless block equal to the complete independent color-one class, and that class must dominate. The converse constructions prove the exact dichotomy. Injection counting gives the identity; linear independence of falling factorials gives reconstruction and optimizer formulas, with all k and empty color-one boundary cases resolved. Independently enumerated 1594 graph-palette-k counts over 440702 assignments across 65 verified graph instances; finite checks corroborate, not replace, the proof.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The familiar \(k=1\) numerical chromatic equality is explicitly subsumed and not claimed new. The stronger identity determines the number of each feasible labeled map for every k and t and implies recovery of both independent-set and maximal-independent-set enumerators, which the established ordinary minimum equality does not imply. The complete 2026 primary document could not be inspected, so a covert equivalent lemma cannot be ruled out.

An equivalent result would require an exact per-coloring test for all k or the full enumeration, not merely a chromatic minimum. No such implication was found in accessible material; the originating preprint remains a specific unresolved full-text comparison risk.

value.rationale: Natural all-coloring enumeration for a newly defined graph coloring invariant over every finite connected diameter-at-most-two graph, with an exact criterion on broadcast-block feasibility. The falling-factorial coefficients reconstruct the entire independent-set size enumerator and the entire maximal-independent-set size enumerator, a qualitative gain beyond a minimum alone, and establish an exact optimum multiplicity plus a structural high-k gap/plateau transition. Not an arbitrary finite slice or a routine renaming of the old chromatic bound.
